newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian Feb trade surplus seen unsustainable.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian Feb trade surplus seen unsustainable.

text.p: Malaysia on Tuesday reported a trade surplus of 367.2 million ringgit ($146.3 million) for February, but economists said higher import bills would move the country into deficit over the next few months.
The February data compared with deficits of 102.9 million ringgit in January and 736 million ringgit in the same month last year, the statistics department said.

Economists said that while the surplus was encouraging, the positive data was unlikely to be sustainable in coming months as Malaysia continues to import capital goods and "lumpy items" like aircraft and ships to feed its economic growth.
The data did not move financial markets, with the ringgit largely steady and the stock market stuck in its current doldrums.
The department, which releases the figures on a monthly basis, said exports in February totalled 13.51 billion ringgit against imports of 13.15 billion.

Including February, Malaysia's trade balance for the first two months was a surplus of 264.3 million ringgit, a big improvement from a shortfall of 1.9 billion recorded in the same period a year ago, the department said.

Research house MMS International in Singapore said: "The surplus of 367 million ringgit for February's trade is undoubtedly good news but it is just a notch above what the market has factored in, i.e. a small deficit to surplus of 300 million ringgit."
Economists said a surplus in February was a little out of the ordinary as import bills during the month usually surge due to the Chinese New Year and the Moslem Eid al-Fitr festivals.
"February is usually a deficit because of seasonality, so this will be taken as positive. But whether it is sustainable is questionable," Kevin Chew, economist at Caspian Securities, said.

Import of aircraft and ships by the national carrier Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) and shipping firm Malaysian International Shipping Corp Bhd (MISC) will drag the monthly trade data into deficit again, he said.
"MAS is taking delivery of planes and MISC is importing ships. It's a matter of magnitude of how much it (the data) will worsen," said Chew.
Mustafa Mohd Nor, chief economist at Arab Malaysian Securities, noted the February data indicated that the speed of private capital formation growth was not picking up.
"The market is actually looking for a higher import figure as an indication that private capital formation is picking up and growth is being sustained," Mustafa said.
"March numbers from Singapore are also showing this weak trend." ($1=2.51 ringgit)
